newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Milburn sees healthy construction outlook.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Milburn sees healthy construction outlook.

text.p: Cement maker Milburn New Zealand Ltd said on Monday that higher infrastructure spending planned by the new centre-right coalition government would underpin the construction sector for much of 1997, and activity was expected to remain healthy into next year.
Milburn earlier reported a rise in net profit for the year to December 31 to NZ$24.3 million from $22.8 million.
Operating profit, excluding Chinese operations, was up 15.7 percent at $49.9 million, more than double the level of three years ago.
It said cement, concerete, aggregate and lime sales in New Zealand were strong throughout the year.
"Despite a moderate slowdown in overall economic growth, building authorisations were considerably ahead of the previous year," it said.
Local authority and private investment in infrastructure was expected to continue around the current "satisfactory" levels.

"Inflationary pressures may develop towards the end of 1997, leading to a corrective action by the Reserve Bank, with higher interest rates and thus a slowdown in some sectors of the economy," Milburn said.
"Construction activity is expected to remain healthy into 1998, but emerging trends will be closely monitored in order to take corrective action where necessary."
The group would continue to focus on improving performance in cost-efficient production and distribution, effective marketing and superior service and quality.
"It will be ready to take advantage of opportunities which arise in its core business areas of cement, concrete, aggregate and lime," the company said.
